samples.summary: Three CLI error emitters were left unattributed while the diff added `command` everywhere else
samples.evidence: The diff threads `this` into `outputError`/`forwardUpstreamError` for every data command and adds `command` to the documented envelope (docs/design/cli.md §8.1, line 898: `"command": "docs.content"`). Three call sites in the same actions were missed and still emit an envelope with no `command`: `packages/cli/src/commands/ctx.ts:85` (`ctx list`, inside `function (this: Command)` at :71), `packages/cli/src/commands/status.ts:69` (`status`, action at :61), and `packages/cli/src/commands/cells.ts:139` (the `sheets cells batch` invalid-JSON path — the sibling case at `tabs.ts:42` *was* updated in this diff). An agent driving several calls therefore gets attribution for most failures but not for these, i.e. the contract is applied inconsistently across the surface the diff claims to cover.

samples.summary: Making cookie names env-dependent leaves pre-existing specs (and oauth-state.spec) reading the bare names without pinning the env
samples.evidence: Before this change the names were module constants (`ACCESS_COOKIE_NAME`/`REFRESH_COOKIE_NAME`), so specs were env-independent. They now come from `sessionCookieName()` → `isSecureCookie()`, which reads `COOKIE_SECURE` and `GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL` (packages/backend/src/auth/oauth-state.ts:230-238). The diff adds `delete process.env.GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL` only inside the new describes, leaving the older cases that assert bare names env-fragile: `packages/backend/src/auth/auth.controller.spec.ts:68-75` (logout), :104-113 (refresh), :127-134, :730 and :757 (JwtStrategy cookie extraction), and `packages/backend/src/auth/oauth-state.spec.ts:66/78`. On a machine exporting `GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL=https://…` or `COOKIE_SECURE=true` these now fail while CI stays green — precisely the hazard the diff's own comments describe, fixed only for the new blocks.

samples.summary: rest-api.md still describes the CLI Continue link as carrying the confirm cookie secret, and `__Host-` as production-only
samples.evidence: `docs/design/rest-api.md:464-468` says the Continue link "carries a one-time secret that also went out as an httpOnly `__Host-wafflebase_cli_confirm` cookie … unprefixed only outside production". Both halves are now wrong: the link carries `cliConfirmToken(secret, port, nonce, challenge)` (packages/backend/src/auth/cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts:164), never the cookie value, and the prefix/`Secure` decision is `useSecureCookies()` — `COOKIE_SECURE`, then the callback URL's scheme, with `NODE_ENV` only as fallback (oauth-state.ts:229-239), so a `NODE_ENV=production` install with an `http://` callback is now unprefixed. backend.md was updated (line 494) but this doc was not; content drift in design docs is unchecked by CI.

samples.summary: backend README still documents unprefixed session cookies and the confirm cookie secret as the `?confirm=` value
samples.evidence: `packages/backend/README.md:452` — "Tokens are set as httpOnly cookies (`wafflebase_session`, `wafflebase_refresh`)" — predates `sessionCookieName()`/`refreshCookieName()`, which now emit `__Host-`-prefixed names wherever cookies are `Secure`. `README.md:461` likewise says the click "carries the `__Host-wafflebase_cli_confirm` cookie secret back as `?confirm=`", which is no longer true after `cliConfirmToken` (cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts:97).

samples.summary: `login_state` error code added to the frontend map is never emitted by the backend, and its justifying comment is unsupported by the repo
samples.evidence: The only login redirect codes the backend produces are `oauth_state` (packages/backend/src/auth/auth.controller.ts:149 and :167 via `loginErrorUrl('oauth_state')`); a grep for `login_state` across the repo finds it only in the new frontend map and its new test. The comment at login-form.tsx:22-24 claims "the two names for the same refusal have both been in the callback's vocabulary", which no producer in the tree supports — a dead branch plus a doc claim a future reader will trust.

samples.summary: Two new login tests do not point `WAFFLEBASE_CONFIG` at a temp dir, so `announceLoginUrl` writes into the developer's real config directory
samples.evidence: `announceLoginUrl` (packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts) writes `login-url.txt` beside `getConfigPath()` whenever stderr is not a TTY — always true under vitest. The first test in the `wafflebase login` describe sets `process.env.WAFFLEBASE_CONFIG` (and `login.test.ts`/`login-command.test.ts` were updated to do so), but the 401 and 502 cases (login-callback.test.ts:366 and :443 register the command and only set `WAFFLEBASE_SESSION`) leave it unset, so the suite mkdir/writes/removes a file under the real `~/.wafflebase` on a developer machine.

samples.summary: Comment still says the callback wait is "now three minutes" after CALLBACK_TIMEOUT_MS became five
samples.evidence: packages/cli/test/login-listen-failure.test.ts:12 documents the default wait as "(now three minutes)"; `CALLBACK_TIMEOUT_MS` is now `5 * 60 * 1000` (packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts). The test itself passes an explicit `timeoutMs: 50`, so only the comment is wrong.

finding.summary: Reviewer did not produce a valid verdict: review: every credential in the pool (2) was retired — nothing left to fail over to

verdict.reason: The finding text is the panel's synthetic no-verdict record, not a code claim: scripts/agent/ask.mjs:630-637 (poolExhaustedError) produces the exact "every credential in the pool (N) was retired — nothing left to fail over to" message, and scripts/agent/review-panel.mjs:1690-1696 wraps a non-infra error as "Reviewer did not produce a valid verdict: <message>". It means the blast-radius lens itself never completed. I cannot refute it: it names no file, symbol or bypassing call site, so no refutation ground (not-present / already-guarded / counterexample) can be anchored to code the finding described. Moreover the repo's own design treats this exact record as a deliberate fail-closed blocker — review-panel.mjs:1684-1689 distinguishes infra failures ("must never be re-checked as a code finding") from a genuine no-verdict which "IS an ordinary fail-closed blocker", and review-round-guard.mjs:186-190 pages a human on the invalid-verdict path. Dropping it would remove the only signal that this lens did not run. Whether pool exhaustion should instead have been classified as infra (ask.mjs sets kind="pool-exhausted", not err.infra) is unresolved ambiguity, which by rule keeps the finding.
